name: is-this-difference-real
query: Group A averaged 4.1 and group B averaged 4.8 on the same task. Is that difference real or am I reading noise?
why: The core domain-free question. Must fire with no domain context at all, and the answer is an effect size with an interval plus a permutation test, not a bare p-value.

name: how-big-a-sample
query: How many responses do I need before I can tell whether the new version is better?
why: Sample size and power. The skill's job is to get the minimum effect worth detecting stated first, since without it the question has no answer.

name: is-this-streak-meaningful
query: I've won seven in a row. Does that mean anything or is it just what chance looks like?
why: Domain-free streak question. Runs occur in random sequences far more often than intuition allows, and the streak was noticed because it was extreme.

name: what-does-this-correlation-tell-me
query: These two columns have a correlation of 0.62. What does that actually tell me?
why: Correlation interpretation - r-squared as the share of variance, the disqualifiers (outliers, nonlinearity, restricted range), and the refusal to use causal language on observational data.

name: audit-a-writeup
query: Can you check this analysis before I send it? It says the improvement was significant at p equals 0.03.
why: The auditor case. A p-value with no effect size, no interval and no n is three named defects, and the skill should report them by code rather than warning vaguely.

name: outlier-or-real
query: A few values in this column are way bigger than the rest. Should I drop them?
why: Robust statistics and outlier handling. The answer depends on what the outlier is for, and the skill must refuse silent deletion.

name: small-sample-interval
query: I only have 12 measurements. Can I still say anything useful about the average?
why: Interval on a small sample, where the honest contribution is reporting the width. Domain-free and a common real moment.

name: threshold-for-a-data-check
query: What threshold should this data quality check fire at? Right now it's three sigma and it alerts every single day.
why: The threshold handoff. Where the check runs belongs to data-engineering; how the number is chosen is this skill, and three sigma on skewed data is the canonical failure.

name: var-on-returns
query: What's the value at risk on this returns series over a ten day horizon?
why: Market risk as calculation. Requires the confidence level, horizon and estimation window stated, and empirical rather than normal quantiles because of fat tails.

name: did-my-model-actually-improve
query: My new model scores 0.91 against the old one's 0.89. Did it actually improve?
why: Evaluation as inference - paired comparison on the same test set, bootstrap interval on the difference, and the count of configurations tried.

name: is-this-bet-plus-ev
query: The price is 2.10 and I think the true probability is about 52 percent. Is that a positive expected value bet?
why: Edge and expected value as arithmetic. The skill computes it, puts an interval on the probability estimate, and does not tell anyone to place or size a bet.

name: backtest-too-good
query: My backtest returns 40 percent a year. What should I check before I believe it?
why: Backtest honesty - look-ahead, survivorship, costs, and above all how many parameter combinations were tried before this one was reported.

name: leaky-metric
query: My classifier gets 99.8 percent accuracy on the holdout. That seems too good.
why: Leakage detected in a result, which is this skill's half of that boundary. The answer is the leakage catalog and a check on what each feature knows at prediction time.

name: pipeline-load-strategy
query: Should I load this source incrementally with a merge or just do a full refresh every night?
why: Platform and ingestion mechanics belong to data-engineering. No inference question is present, and firing here would poach a sibling's trigger.

name: where-quality-checks-go
query: Where in the pipeline should our quality checks run, and which ones should block the load?
why: Placement and blocking policy belong to data-engineering. The deliberate contrast with the threshold case - this skill owns how the number is chosen, not where the check sits.

name: warehouse-modeling
query: Should one row of my sales fact table be an order or an order line?
why: Grain is dimensional modeling. Adjacent vocabulary (rows, tables, measures) makes it a plausible false positive.

name: which-model-to-train
query: Which algorithm should I use for this classification problem, and how do I engineer the features?
why: Model building - framing, features, training - is machine-learning's half. This skill treats a model as an instrument to measure, not an artifact to construct.

name: chart-request
query: Make me a chart showing revenue by region over the last four quarters.
why: Visualization belongs to dataviz. No question about whether a number is real, only about how it is drawn.

name: plain-arithmetic
query: Add up column C in this spreadsheet and give me the total.
why: A computation with no inference in it. Guards against firing on anything numeric.
